Establish ethical boundaries for AI surveillance. Require ethics review for new monitoring AI deployments. Comply with workplace surveillance laws and ECPA requirements.
controls.risk_statement: Unconstrained AI surveillance damages employee trust, customer relationships, and creates legal liability under workplace and consumer privacy laws.

controls.objective_text: Technical standards require that all AI models deployed in production undergo peer code review, automated testing, and security scanning before deployment approval.
controls.implementation_guidance: Mandate peer code review for all AI model code before deployment. Implement automated testing suites covering unit tests, integration tests, and performance benchmarks. Require security scanning of AI code and dependencies. Integrate these checks into CI/CD pipelines with deployment blocking on failure. Document review and testing results. Track code review quality metrics.
controls.risk_statement: Deploying AI code without peer review and testing increases the risk of bugs, security vulnerabilities, and operational failures in production.

controls.objective_text: Risk identification for AI used in payments, clearing, and settlement includes assessment of latency risk, throughput limitations, and potential for AI failures to disrupt financial market infrastructure.
controls.implementation_guidance: Conduct specialized risk identification for AI in payment and settlement systems. Assess: maximum latency thresholds before transaction failures, throughput capacity under peak conditions, single-point-of-failure risks, and potential cascading effects on SIFMU counterparties. Include stress scenarios for simultaneous high-volume and model degradation events. Coordinate with treasury and operations risk functions.
controls.risk_statement: AI failures in payment infrastructure can cause cascading settlement failures affecting the broader financial system.

controls.objective_text: The organization implements ongoing bias monitoring for production AI systems, tracking fairness metrics over time and alerting when bias indicators exceed defined thresholds.
controls.implementation_guidance: Deploy continuous fairness monitoring for all consumer-facing AI systems. Calculate fairness metrics on production data at defined intervals (daily for high-risk, weekly for medium). Set alert thresholds for fairness metric degradation. Implement automated reporting of fairness trends. Trigger investigation when alerts fire. Report fairness monitoring results to fair lending compliance. Include in governance committee reporting.
controls.risk_statement: Pre-deployment fairness testing alone is insufficient — bias can emerge or shift over time as populations and data distributions change in production.

controls.objective_text: The organization conducts stress testing of AI credit risk models under macroeconomic scenarios aligned with CCAR, DFAST, and internal stress testing programs.
controls.implementation_guidance: Integrate AI credit models into enterprise stress testing. Apply supervisory scenarios (severely adverse, adverse, baseline) to AI model inputs. Measure model performance degradation under stressed conditions. Compare AI model stress results to traditional model results. Assess whether AI models amplify or dampen procyclical effects. Document stress testing methodology and results per CCAR/DFAST requirements.
controls.risk_statement: AI credit models not stress-tested may understate losses under adverse scenarios, potentially leading to insufficient capital reserves.

controls.objective_text: Fairness testing for AI in insurance underwriting evaluates compliance with state insurance regulations, unfair discrimination prohibitions, and rate-filing requirements where AI influences pricing or eligibility.
controls.implementation_guidance: Conduct fairness analysis specific to insurance regulatory requirements. Evaluate AI underwriting and pricing models for unfair discrimination under state insurance laws. Assess compliance with prohibited factor restrictions by state. Ensure AI-influenced rates are supportable in rate filings. Coordinate with insurance compliance and actuarial functions. Document analysis for department of insurance examination.
controls.risk_statement: AI in insurance underwriting that produces unfairly discriminatory outcomes violates state insurance laws and risks rate disapproval and enforcement actions.

controls.objective_text: The organization provides clear, plain-language explanations of AI-driven decisions to consumers when required by law or regulation, including credit decisions, insurance determinations, and employment actions.
controls.implementation_guidance: Develop consumer-facing explanation capabilities for AI systems subject to disclosure requirements. Generate plain-language explanations that are: specific to the individual decision, accurate regarding the key factors, actionable for the consumer, and compliant with regulatory requirements (ECOA, FCRA, state AI laws). Test consumer comprehension. Maintain explanation logs for audit. Update explanation formats as regulatory guidance evolves.
controls.risk_statement: Failure to provide adequate explanations of AI decisions to consumers violates existing consumer protection laws and emerging AI-specific disclosure requirements.

controls.objective_text: The organization implements specific security controls for generative AI systems, including prompt injection defenses, output filtering, and controls preventing unauthorized data access through conversational AI interfaces.
controls.implementation_guidance: Deploy GenAI-specific security controls: input sanitization to prevent prompt injection, output filtering to prevent data leakage and harmful content, session isolation to prevent cross-user data exposure, rate limiting to prevent automated abuse, and access controls ensuring AI only accesses authorized data. Conduct regular red team exercises targeting GenAI systems. Monitor for novel GenAI attack vectors.
controls.risk_statement: Generative AI systems present unique security attack surfaces that traditional application security controls do not adequately address.

controls.objective_text: The organization evaluates AI vendors' data privacy practices, ensuring third-party AI processing of customer data complies with GLBA safeguards requirements and contractual data handling obligations.
controls.implementation_guidance: Assess vendor AI data privacy practices through due diligence questionnaires and audits. Verify GLBA compliance for all vendors processing NPI in AI systems. Include data handling requirements in vendor contracts. Monitor vendor compliance with contractual data obligations. Assess risk of vendor data aggregation across clients. Implement data minimization principles in vendor AI engagements.
controls.risk_statement: Vendor AI processing of customer data without adequate privacy controls creates GLBA violations and data breach risk for the financial institution.

controls.objective_text: The organization develops and maintains contingency plans for AI model failure that include predefined fallback strategies, manual override procedures, and communication templates for stakeholder notification.
controls.implementation_guidance: Create contingency plans for each critical AI system. Include: predefined fallback processing (manual, rules-based, or prior model version), communication templates for customer notification, regulatory notification procedures, business line impact mitigation steps, and restoration criteria. Test contingency plans through simulation exercises. Ensure plans are accessible to operations staff 24/7. Review and update annually.
controls.risk_statement: AI system failures without contingency plans result in prolonged service disruptions, ad hoc responses, and delayed stakeholder communication.

controls.objective_text: The organization tracks and manages technical debt in AI systems, preventing accumulation of shortcuts and deferred improvements that increase long-term risk.
controls.implementation_guidance: Inventory and track AI technical debt: outdated dependencies, deprecated features, deferred refactoring, missing tests, and documentation gaps. Assess risk impact of accumulated technical debt. Allocate dedicated capacity for technical debt reduction (e.g., 20% of AI engineering capacity). Prioritize debt remediation based on risk and cost of delay. Report technical debt levels to governance committee. Prevent critical debt accumulation.
controls.risk_statement: AI technical debt silently increases fragility and operational risk, eventually leading to costly failures or forced rewrites.

controls.objective_text: The organization maintains a register of AI-related operational losses and near-misses, integrating AI events into the enterprise operational risk loss database for comprehensive risk assessment.
controls.implementation_guidance: Record AI-related operational losses in the enterprise loss database. Capture: direct financial losses, remediation costs, regulatory fines, and opportunity costs. Track near-misses that could have resulted in losses. Categorize by AI risk type for trend analysis. Use loss data to calibrate AI risk models and capital assessments. Report to operational risk committee and board. Benchmark loss experience against industry data.
controls.risk_statement: AI operational losses not captured in the enterprise loss database distort the organization's understanding of total operational risk exposure.

controls.objective_text: The organization ensures clear separation of duties between AI system development, validation, and deployment approval functions, preventing conflicts of interest in AI governance.
controls.implementation_guidance: Enforce separation of duties: developers cannot validate their own models, model owners cannot approve deployment without independent sign-off, and validation findings cannot be overridden by development leadership. Document organizational structure supporting separation of duties. Verify separation is maintained for third-party AI through contractual and oversight mechanisms. Audit separation of duties compliance annually.
controls.risk_statement: Conflicted AI governance where developers self-approve systems undermines independent oversight and is a fundamental SR 11-7 deficiency.

controls.objective_text: The organization identifies and manages concentration risk in AI, including dependency on single AI platforms, shared model architectures, or common training datasets across multiple AI systems.
controls.implementation_guidance: Assess AI concentration risk across: technology platforms (single cloud provider), model architectures (all systems using one approach), data sources (common training data across models), and vendor concentration. Quantify the potential impact of concentrated failures. Develop diversification strategies for critical concentrations. Implement monitoring for concentration risk indicators. Report concentration risk to governance committee.
controls.risk_statement: AI concentration creates correlated failure risk that could simultaneously affect multiple business functions.

controls.objective_text: The organization documents assumptions about the operating environment that underpin AI system design, and monitors for changes in these assumptions that could invalidate model performance.
controls.implementation_guidance: Catalog key assumptions for each AI system: data distribution stability, regulatory environment, market conditions, customer behavior patterns, and technology infrastructure. Define monitoring approaches for each assumption. Set triggers for assumption review when operating environment changes materially. Link assumption violations to model revalidation triggers. Document assumption monitoring in ongoing monitoring plans.
controls.risk_statement: AI systems designed under assumptions that no longer hold produce unreliable outputs, but this degradation is invisible without explicit assumption monitoring.

controls.objective_text: The organization measures and manages the cost efficiency of AI operations, tracking inference costs, infrastructure utilization, and return on AI investment across the portfolio.
controls.implementation_guidance: Track AI operational costs at system level: compute costs, data storage, API calls, infrastructure maintenance, and human oversight costs. Calculate cost per prediction/inference. Monitor cost trends and anomalies. Compare costs to business value delivered. Optimize: right-size infrastructure, implement model efficiency improvements, and consolidate redundant capabilities. Report AI cost efficiency metrics to finance and governance committee.
controls.risk_statement: Unmanaged AI operational costs can erode the business case for AI investments and divert resources from higher-value initiatives.

controls.objective_text: Post-deployment monitoring for AI in BSA/AML transaction monitoring includes assessment of suspicious activity detection rates, false positive rates, and investigation efficiency impacts.
controls.implementation_guidance: Monitor BSA/AML AI performance metrics: SAR filing rates, true positive rates, false positive rates, investigation time savings, and typology coverage. Compare AI-augmented detection to historical rules-based detection. Track regulatory feedback on AI-influenced SARs. Monitor for changes in transaction patterns that may indicate model drift. Report BSA/AML AI performance to BSA Officer and governance committee.
controls.risk_statement: BSA/AML AI that degrades detection capability without monitoring may result in BSA compliance failures and FinCEN enforcement actions.

controls.objective_text: The organization assesses AI-human handoff processes in customer service contexts, measuring whether transitions between AI and human agents are seamless and do not degrade customer experience.
controls.implementation_guidance: Measure AI-human handoff quality: customer wait time during transfer, context preservation (does the human agent have AI interaction history), customer satisfaction with the transition, resolution rate post-handoff, and abandonment rate during handoff. Optimize handoff triggers to balance AI efficiency with customer needs. Test handoff processes regularly. Collect and analyze customer feedback on AI-human transitions.
controls.risk_statement: Poor AI-human handoffs frustrate customers, increase call handling time, and erode trust in the institution's service quality.

controls.objective_text: The organization establishes shared infrastructure and platforms for AI development and deployment that promote consistency, efficiency, and governance compliance across AI teams.
controls.implementation_guidance: Invest in centralized AI platforms providing: standardized development environments, shared feature stores, model registry, automated MLOps pipelines, and monitoring infrastructure. Embed governance controls into the platform (automated validation checks, documentation requirements, approval workflows). Enable self-service AI development within guardrails. Track platform adoption and governance compliance metrics.
controls.risk_statement: Fragmented AI infrastructure leads to inconsistent practices, duplicated effort, and difficulty enforcing governance standards across teams.

controls.objective_text: The organization ensures AI-driven customer communications and disclosures are accurate, not misleading, and compliant with UDAAP, Truth in Lending, and other consumer protection requirements.
controls.implementation_guidance: Review all AI-generated customer communications for accuracy and compliance before deployment. Test generative AI outputs against UDAAP standards (not unfair, deceptive, or abusive). Verify compliance with TILA, Reg Z, and other disclosure requirements for AI-generated financial content. Implement output validation and filtering for compliance-sensitive communications. Monitor production outputs for compliance drift.
controls.risk_statement: AI-generated communications that are inaccurate or misleading violate consumer protection laws and create UDAAP enforcement risk.

controls.objective_text: The organization implements data loss prevention controls for AI systems that prevent unauthorized transfer or exposure of sensitive training data, model parameters, and inference results.
controls.implementation_guidance: Implement DLP controls tailored to AI data flows. Monitor for unauthorized data transfers of: training datasets, model weights and parameters, customer inference results, and feature store data. Apply network-level DLP for AI development and serving environments. Control data egress from AI systems. Prevent unauthorized copying of model artifacts. Integrate AI DLP with enterprise DLP program.
controls.risk_statement: AI systems without DLP controls risk unauthorized data exposure, model theft, and regulatory violations for data handling failures.

controls.objective_text: AI risk communication strategies address the specific needs of regulatory examination teams, with pre-prepared materials that clearly explain AI systems, governance processes, and risk management practices.
controls.implementation_guidance: Develop examination readiness packages for AI systems. Include: AI inventory overviews, governance framework summaries, model documentation indexes, validation report summaries, monitoring dashboards, and issue status reports. Assign designated examination liaisons with AI expertise. Conduct pre-examination readiness drills. Maintain materials in up-to-date, regulator-accessible format. Brief examination teams proactively on AI program developments.
controls.risk_statement: Poorly prepared examination responses for AI create unfavorable impressions with regulators and extend examination timelines with follow-up requests.

controls.objective_text: The organization's AI strategy addresses the unique risks and opportunities of agentic AI systems — AI that can take autonomous actions, use tools, and chain multi-step reasoning — with enhanced governance for autonomous decision-making.
controls.implementation_guidance: Develop governance frameworks for agentic AI that address: scope of permitted autonomous actions, guardrails and boundaries, monitoring of autonomous behavior chains, approval requirements for tool use and external system access, and human oversight escalation triggers. Assess agentic AI risks including: unintended action chains, cascading errors, and unauthorized scope expansion. Define deployment criteria specific to agentic systems.
controls.risk_statement: Agentic AI systems that take autonomous actions without adequate governance can cause cascading harm that is difficult to detect and reverse.

controls.objective_text: AI risk reporting to the board includes clear articulation of the AI risk-return trade-off, enabling informed board decisions about the pace and scope of AI adoption.
controls.implementation_guidance: Frame board AI reporting in risk-return terms the board can act on. Present: AI business value delivered against risk costs, risk trend direction (improving/stable/deteriorating), regulatory readiness assessment, and key decisions requiring board input. Provide comparative context (industry trends, peer benchmarks). Avoid excessive technical jargon. Include forward-looking risk projections. Enable the board to make informed decisions on AI strategy and appetite.
controls.risk_statement: Board reporting that is either too technical or too abstract fails to support informed governance, resulting in either uninformed approval or excessive caution.

controls.objective_text: The organization assesses AI's impact on operational resilience, evaluating whether AI adoption increases or decreases the institution's ability to absorb and recover from operational disruptions.
controls.implementation_guidance: Evaluate AI's net effect on operational resilience. Assess: does AI create new single points of failure? Does AI improve processing flexibility? Can AI-dependent processes recover from disruptions? Is AI infrastructure diversified across failure domains? Include AI in operational resilience scenario testing per regulatory expectations. Document AI resilience assessment in operational resilience framework.
controls.risk_statement: AI that improves efficiency but reduces resilience creates hidden fragility that manifests during operational stress events.

controls.objective_text: The organization establishes model performance benchmarks that are updated with each retraining cycle, enabling longitudinal tracking of model effectiveness and early detection of secular performance trends.
controls.implementation_guidance: Maintain historical performance benchmarks for each model across retraining cycles. Track key metrics over time to identify secular trends (gradual improvement or degradation). Compare each retrained model to: initial deployment performance, previous version, and peer models for similar use cases. Use longitudinal data to inform retraining frequency decisions. Alert when performance trends indicate approaching risk thresholds.
controls.risk_statement: Without longitudinal benchmarks, organizations cannot distinguish between normal variation and concerning performance trends that warrant intervention.
